title: Dot-Star Matching
statement:
Decide whether a tiny pattern language describes an entire word.

Contract
- `text` is a non-null string of lowercase letters (possibly empty).
- `pattern` is a non-null string made of lowercase letters, `.` and `*`. A `*` always follows a letter or a `.` and never starts the pattern or follows another `*`.
- `.` matches any single letter. A letter matches itself. `x*` matches zero or more copies of the element `x` that comes right before the star (so `.*` matches any run of letters).
- The pattern must match the WHOLE text, not just a prefix or a substring. Return `true` or `false`.

Examples
- `matches("moon", "mo*n")` returns `true` (`o*` covers both `o`).
- `matches("moon", "mo.")` returns `false` because the pattern ends one letter early.
- `matches("", "a*b*")` returns `true` because both starred elements can match nothing.
hints: Look at the pattern one element at a time; a starred element gives you a choice between using it zero times and using it once more.

Let `ok[i][j]` mean the first `i` letters of the text match the first `j` characters of the pattern. For `x*`, either skip it (`ok[i][j-2]`) or consume a letter that `x` matches and stay on the star (`ok[i-1][j]`).

Row `i` only needs row `i-1`, so two boolean rows suffice. Remember the empty-text row, where every `x*` pair can vanish. Intended complexity: O(n*m) time and O(m) space for a text of length n and a pattern of length m; the workload uses n = m.
inputSyntax: Input: a lowercase text, a comma, then a pattern of letters, . and *, for example: moon, mo*n
